summary: Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at the University of London. She taught at Kurukshetra University, University of Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is an academic in religious studies, philosophy, and management. He studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (1991–1997) and San Francisco State University (~1997).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He taught at Harvard (~1978–1987), Wellesley College (~1987–1990), University of California, Santa Barbara (~1994–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick was an Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oxford under Harold Walter Bailey (~1961–1964) and was a professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley (1985). He studied under numerous teachers and held an attested post at Fairfield University (2002–2005).
Ronald Neufeldt is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held faculty positions in the Religious Studies Department at the University of Calgary, attested around 1977 and 2001.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1986) and Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a Sinologist, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and served on the faculty at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rong Ma is a sociologist and Tibetologist who earned a doctorate in social geography at Brown University. He served as Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University (attested 1998) and was a visiting scholar at Harvard.

Rongdao Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She received her Ph.D. from McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University, where Leonard van der Kuijp was his doctoral supervisor.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and taught at International Christian College.

Rosalind O'Hanlon is a historian and Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London (~1977–1982). She held posts at Clare College, Cambridge (~1979–2001) and the University of Oxford (~2001–2020).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served there as research assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1983–2012), and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher and earned an MA at Free University of Brussels. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970).

Rosemarie Fuchs is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Katia Holmes and traditional teacher Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. She held professorships at the University of Giessen (1990–1994) and University of Jena (1994–2013), and was an honorary professor at Humboldt University (2013).
